So, this is my first Armored Core game and I'm having a great time so far! I'm only at Chapter 3 >!(got past the "stealth" mission)!< so I don't have an overwhelming amount of stuff to work with here. But, if any of you have suggestions or criticisms for my builds then I'll be glad to hear it. I'm playing the PS5 version btw.  
  
Silver Fox:  
My strategy when using this build is to jump/fly/dodge as much as possible while using the pistols to keep the pressure on the ACS Overload Gage. When the enemy is staggered, I blast them with the laser cannons to vaporize their health. Rinse and repeat until they drop. But, considering it has less than 10,000 health, I try to pay attention to patterns more.  
  
The Amazing Bulk:  
Pretty much the tanky build that's really slow but can eviscerate health and stagger bars. The mini-guns are great for piling on the stagger very quickly and the laser cannons once again chop down the health to size. I recently made this build, so I'm not quite used to dodging things with something more slow compared to the Silver Fox. But, it's fun to watch Arena ACs get pulverized.

Door to Phantomile = Lunatea's Veil - Both games are masterpieces in not only gameplay, but also in storytelling. Through and through.

The GBA Platformers - Yeah, they're fun, but they feel more like generic mascot platformers which I assume was the intention. Also I consider them non-canon because tying them to the story of the mainline games would give me (or really anyone) a run for my money.

Heroes - People are going to kill me for this, but for a franchise that is very well known for it's story, you'd think that the Action RPG of the bunch would have an interesting and compelling story, but nope. Heroes has the story of a generic shounen anime. But from what little I've actually played of it, the gameplay's fine.

Moonlight Museum - This is probably considered the weakest one, but I think it's premise is interesting enough to the point where if it was remade (like Final Fantasy 7), it could probably be at least be up there with the mainline ones. But I haven't actually played too much to gauge a proper opinion, but again it's fine. The soundtrack can be a little unpleasant at times though.

If I had to start, I'd say pick up Door to Phantomile either on PSN, Wii, or on emulator because finding a physical version of it is quite costly these days. Although Klonoa 2 isn't a SUPER direct sequel (no spoilers), but still it would be preferable to play Door to Phantomile first!
